prompt: Six machines of the order API sit in a set with two fault domains and five update domains. The power supply feeding one rack fails. What does the shop lose?
hint: A rack is a row in the figure, not a column.

choices.text: One machine, the one whose update domain was due for a restart
choices.why: That describes planned maintenance, which takes an update domain. A power failure is unplanned and takes a fault domain.

choices.text: The machines of that fault domain, three of the six
choices.why: Right. A fault domain is the hardware that shares a power source and a switch, so its machines go together, and the other fault domain keeps answering.

choices.text: Nothing, because Azure moves the six to another rack before the power goes
choices.why: A power supply that dies gives no notice. Live migration moves a machine off a host that is still running, not off a rack whose power has already gone.

choices.text: All six, since an availability set lives inside one rack
choices.why: The set exists to spread its machines across fault domains, which are different racks' worth of power and network.

prompt: A set has five update domains. Twelve machines are created in it, one after another. How many machines are in the first machine's update domain, counting the first one?
hint: The sixth goes with the first, the seventh with the second.

prompt: `shop-web-1` has run on its own for a month. The team now wants it in `shop-avset`. What does that take?
hint: Read the SDK's description of `availabilitySet` again.

choices.text: Adding `availabilitySet` to the running machine's file and deploying it again
choices.why: The property is accepted only when the machine is created. An existing machine cannot be added to a set.

choices.text: Deallocating it first, then setting the property and starting it
choices.why: Deallocating does not reopen the choice. It is also the step that can put two machines of a set in one fault domain.

choices.text: A new machine, created in the set
choices.why: Right. A machine joins a set when it is created or never, so the way in is a new machine there.

choices.text: Raising the set's fault domain count so that there is room for it
choices.why: The counts are fixed once the set exists, and they are not a capacity limit on the number of machines.

prompt: In Bicep, a managed availability set, the kind that holds machines with managed disks, is declared with the `sku` name ___.
hint: It is the word for disks that follow their machine's fault domain.

prompt: Put in order what happens to a set during a planned maintenance that needs a reboot.
hint: Notice comes first; the update domains come last.
items: During the self-service phase, you may start it on a machine yourself
The scheduled phase begins, and Azure starts it
That update domain has 30 minutes to recover before the next one starts
trap: The 30 minutes come after a restart, not before it: they are the time a restarted update domain has to recover.

prompt: The shop's two machines are created in Brazil South with no `zones` at all. Which is true of them?
hint: Regional is not the same as everywhere.

choices.text: Each one is spread over the three zones, like a zone-redundant address
choices.why: A machine is never spread by Azure. Without zones it is regional: placed in one zone it does not tell you about.

choices.text: They go into zones 1 and 2, one each, because there are two of them
choices.why: Nothing assigns regional machines to zones in order, and nothing reports which zone they landed in.

choices.text: Azure places each in a zone it does not report, and nothing stops both sharing one
choices.why: Right. A regional machine is in one zone nobody tells you, so nothing keeps two of them apart, and a failure in any zone takes down whichever is in it.

choices.text: They cannot be created, because a region with zones requires one
choices.why: Regional machines are allowed in a region with zones; they simply have no zone of their own that you chose.

prompt: Match each declaration to what it gives the shop.
hint: Zonal, zone-redundant, regional, and one combination.

pairs.right: Pinned to one zone, and down whenever that zone is
Spread by Azure, surviving the loss of any one zone
In one zone of the region that nobody reports
Compiles cleanly, and is a pair Azure does not accept

right_distractors: Copied by Azure into the region's pair

prompt: The shop's subscription and the finance team's subscription each put a machine in zone `1` of Brazil South, to keep them together. What have they actually arranged?
hint: Who decides which building `1` means?

choices.text: Two machines in one building, since zone 1 is the same for every customer
choices.why: Zone numbers are logical. Each subscription's are mapped to physical zones, and the mapping is returned per subscription.

choices.text: Nothing certain: each subscription maps its zone `1` on its own
choices.why: Right. The location list carries `logicalZone` and `physicalZone` per subscription, and only reading both mappings says whether the two machines share a building.

choices.text: Two different buildings, because Azure keeps subscriptions apart
choices.why: Nothing promises that either. Two subscriptions may map their numbers onto the same physical zone.

choices.text: One building, but only while both deployments use the same API version
choices.why: The API version decides which properties a template may use, not where a zone is.

prompt: Lesson 4's scale set has six instances, two per zone, and the default balancing. Zone 2 goes dark and autoscale adds two instances. Where do they go?
hint: The default is best effort.

choices.text: Nowhere until zone 2 is back, since the scale-out would unbalance the set
choices.why: That is strict balancing, which blocks an operation that would unbalance the set. The default is best effort.

choices.text: Into zone 2, so that each zone keeps the same count
choices.why: Zone 2 is dark; nothing can be created there until it returns.

choices.text: Into the region's pair, which takes over while a zone is down
choices.why: A scale set lives in one region. Nothing moves its instances to another one.

choices.text: Into zones 1 and 3, with the imbalance accepted while zone 2 is down
choices.why: Right. Best effort keeps scaling into the zones that work and accepts the imbalance while one zone is out; later scale operations restore the balance.

prompt: Which of these did the Bicep compiler warn about in this lesson's mistaken copies? Choose all that apply.
hint: It knows types, not limits or combinations.

choices.text: A zone written as the number `1` instead of the string `'1'`
choices.why: Caught: a zone is a string, and each number in the list drew a warning.

choices.text: A machine placed in zone `'4'` of a region with three zones
choices.why: Passed: `'4'` is a string, and the type does not know how many zones a region has.

choices.text: An update domain count written as the text `'5'`
choices.why: Caught: the property is typed as a number, so text drew BCP036.

choices.text: A machine given both a zone and an availability set
choices.why: Passed: each property is valid alone, and the rule against the pair lives in the documentation.

choices.text: Four fault domains on an availability set
choices.why: Passed: four is a number. The limit of three is in Microsoft's documentation, not in the type.

prompt: The agreement measures a virtual machine over 30 days. How many minutes of downtime does a 99.95% promise allow in that period?
hint: 43,200 minutes times what is left over.

prompt: An order passes through the Standard load balancer (99.99%), then the machines across zones (99.99%), then a database promised 99.9%. What is the availability of the chain, in percent, to two decimal places?
hint: In series, multiply the fractions.

prompt: Two copies of a service are each available 99% of the time, and they never fail for the same reason. How many minutes in 30 days are both down at once?
hint: Each is down 0.01 of the time; both together, the product.

prompt: The parallel formula gives two machines of 99.9% an availability of 99.9999%. Why does the agreement promise a pair in an availability set only 99.95%?
hint: Read the formula's assumption.

choices.text: Because it adds the two machines' downtime together instead of multiplying the chances
choices.why: Adding is neither rule. The agreement counts a minute as down when no machine of the set answers.

choices.text: It assumes no shared cause, and the two still share a datacentre
choices.why: Right. Fault domains separate racks, not buildings, so the copies keep failures in common and the agreement does not assume otherwise.

choices.text: Because 99.95% is a figure per machine, so the pair as a whole is promised more
choices.why: The 99.95% is for the set as a whole, two or more machines measured together.

choices.text: The parallel formula is for parts in series, not copies
choices.why: It is the other way round: multiplying availabilities is for parts in series; the parallel formula is for copies.

prompt: One of the shop's two zonal machines is down for a whole day, and the other answers throughout. How much downtime does that day add under the agreement's definition for machines across zones?
hint: When is a minute down for a group of machines?

choices.text: 1,440 minutes, the whole day
choices.why: That would be true of a single machine. Across zones, a minute counts only when no machine in the region answers.

choices.text: 720 minutes, since one machine of two was down
choices.why: The agreement does not count a share of the machines; it asks whether any of them had connectivity.

choices.text: None
choices.why: Right. Downtime across zones is a minute with no connectivity to any machine in the region, and the other one answered all day.

choices.text: It depends on whether the failed machine had Premium SSD disks
choices.why: The disk type decides a single machine's percentage. For machines across zones it does not change what counts as down.

prompt: The order API runs in three zones. Which of these failures does that arrangement not survive?
hint: Look for what every copy has in common.

choices.text: A cooling failure in one of the region's datacentres, lasting an afternoon
choices.why: That is exactly what zones survive: the other two zones have cooling of their own.

choices.text: A release that crashes on start, rolled out to every instance
choices.why: Right. Every copy runs the same image, so a release that breaks it breaks it in all three zones; a rolling upgrade with health checks is what limits that.

choices.text: A rack losing power
choices.why: A rack is smaller than a zone; the instances in other racks and zones keep answering.

choices.text: A maintenance that reboots the machines of the region, zone after zone
choices.why: Maintenance is sequenced zone by zone, so the zones are not all touched at the same moment.

prompt: Why is one machine on Premium SSD a reasonable home for the shop's nightly sales report, when the order API gets three zones?
hint: Ask what a late report costs.

choices.text: Its work is fine late: a failure at two delays a report nobody reads before morning
choices.why: Right. The protection is chosen by the cost of the failure, and here the cost is a late report.

choices.text: A single machine on Premium SSD is promised as much as two machines across zones
choices.why: One machine on Premium SSD is promised 99.9%; two across zones, 99.99%. The report does not need the difference.

choices.text: Reports cannot run on more than one machine
choices.why: Nothing stops it; it would simply cost a second machine for a job that can wait.

choices.text: Night-time hours are outside the SLA's measurement
choices.why: The agreement measures every minute of the 30 days; nothing about the hour changes that.

prompt: Match each failure to what keeps the shop going through it.
hint: Each answer is the size just above the failure.

pairs.right: A copy in a second region
A rolling upgrade that stops when health checks fail

pairs.left: A zone, for one machine's data
pairs.right: A ZRS disk, with a copy in each of three zones

prompt: A team in a region with zones runs two database machines that replicate synchronously, and every write waits for the other machine. Which arrangement fits what it is asking for?
hint: Weigh latency against the size of the failure survived.

choices.text: Two zones, because 99.99% is the highest promise this lesson quotes for machines
choices.why: It survives more, and every write pays the round trip between zones, which this team wants to avoid.

choices.text: A proximity placement group spanning all three zones of the region
choices.why: A proximity placement group is pinned to one datacentre; it cannot span zones.

choices.text: An availability set, accepting that a datacentre failure takes both
choices.why: Right. The set spreads the pair over racks and keeps them close, and a proximity placement group would bring them closer still; the trade is that neither survives the building.

choices.text: One machine with a ZRS disk
choices.why: A ZRS disk keeps the data through a zone failure, but one machine is no replica at all.

prompt: The shop decides to keep a copy of its orders in Brazil South's paired region. What does Microsoft's page on regions say that matters for that copy?
hint: Pairs keep data in one geography, with one exception.

choices.text: The copy stays inside Brazil, as every pair keeps data in its geography
choices.why: Brazil South is the stated exception to that rule.

choices.text: The pair is another zone of Brazil South
choices.why: A pair is a second region. Zones are inside one region.

choices.text: It leaves Brazil: Brazil South's pair is outside its geography
choices.why: Right. The regions page names Brazil South as the exception, so a copy kept in its pair is outside the country.

choices.text: The copy is covered by the 99.99% promise of machines across zones
choices.why: That promise is about machines across zones inside one region. A second region is outside it.

prompt: A copy of `shop-avset.bicep` with `platformFaultDomainCount: 4` compiles with no warning. What does that silence tell you?
hint: What does the compiler know about the property?

choices.text: That Brazil South has four disk fault domains
choices.why: Regions have two or three disk fault domains, and the compiler knows nothing about any region.

choices.text: That the compiler lowers it to the largest count the region allows
choices.why: The template carries the number as written; nothing rewrites it.

choices.text: That 4 is a number, and the limit of three is not in the type
choices.why: Right. The type checks that it is a number and nothing more; the limit is in the documentation, and Resource Manager would refuse the value at deployment.

choices.text: That a Flexible scale set would accept it, so an availability set will too
choices.why: The two are different resources with different documented limits, and neither limit is in the type.

prompt: A single machine on Standard SSD (99.5%) sits behind the Standard load balancer (99.99%). How many minutes of downtime in 30 days do the two promises add up to, to one decimal place?
hint: Multiply the two, then take the rest of 43,200 minutes.

prompt: A virtual machine declared with no `zones` property, in a region that has zones, is called a ___ machine: Azure places it in a zone it does not report.
hint: Not zonal, not zone-redundant.

prompt: In one 30-day period, the order API across zones had 30 minutes in which no machine in the region answered. What does the agreement give the shop?
hint: Turn 30 minutes into a percentage first, then read the credit table.

choices.text: Nothing, since 30 minutes is inside the allowance
choices.why: At 99.99% the allowance is 4.32 minutes. Thirty minutes is about 99.93%, below the promise.

choices.text: A 10% credit on those machines' fees for the period, once it claims within 60 days
choices.why: Right. 99.93% is below 99.99% and above 99%, so the credit is 10%, and only on a claim made within 60 days.

choices.text: A 25% credit, paid automatically
choices.why: 25% is for below 99%, and no credit is automatic: the shop has to claim it.

choices.text: A refund of what the 30 minutes of the shop's machines cost, with an explanation of the cause
choices.why: A credit is a percentage of the period's fees, not the cost of the minutes, and the agreement promises no explanation.
